label: q1-literature
summary: Crossed-design reporter assays give two pictures. Human K562 ExP STARR-seq (1000x1000, GSE184426) finds a multiplicative model with R2=0.82 and high rank agreement across promoters (mean Spearman 0.81 across promoter pairs, 0.72 across enhancer pairs), with a structured minority of deviations (E1 enhancers favour P1 promoters 1.93-fold) and a saturating response at strong, housekeeping-like promoters. Drosophila core-promoter studies (Zabidi 2015) find far stronger specificity: 72% of 11,364 enhancers prefer one of two core promoters by at least 2-fold, and cofactor screens (Haberle 2019) link this to promoter class. Mouse ES-cell MPRAs (Martinez-Ara 2022, 2024) find that over half of enhancers are selective, that strong promoters are boosted less (saturation-like), and that promoters transform summed enhancer input non-linearly. Martinez-Ara's re-analysis of the Bergman data and Bergman's text differ in emphasis, not in data. No study I read gives a per-promoter-pair rank statistic beyond Bergman's means; that would need re-analysis of the GEO tables, which I did not download, so no files were kept.
lay_summary: Think of an enhancer as a volume knob and a promoter as an amplifier. If you try many knobs on one amplifier and then another, the loudest knob is usually still the loudest. A large human experiment found this: about four fifths of the variation fits a simple multiplication of knob times amplifier. In fruit flies, though, most knobs work much better on one of two kinds of amplifier, so the order of strength flips. Mouse studies sit in between: weak amplifiers gain most, strong ones hit a ceiling, and some knobs are picky. So the order mostly changes when promoters belong to different classes, or when a ceiling squashes the strongest enhancers.

glossary.plain: a stretch of DNA that turns up the activity of a gene from a distance
the DNA switch right next to a gene where reading starts
the short stretch, about 100 letters around the start point, where the reading machinery sits
a test where DNA pieces are placed in front of a readable tag and thousands are measured at once
a reporter test where the enhancer itself is read out as RNA
the effect equals enhancer strength times promoter strength
the ranking of enhancers from strongest to weakest
a ceiling where adding more drive gives no more output
a gene needed in every cell, always on
a score from -1 to 1 for how similar two rankings are
the share of the variation a model explains, from 0 to 1
a helper protein that passes the enhancer's signal to the promoter machinery

findings.claim: Bergman 2022 ExP STARR-seq crossed 1,000 enhancers x 1,000 promoters in K562 cells
findings.evidence_quote: applied it to examine the combinatorial compatibilities of 1,000 enhancer and 1,000 promoter sequences in human K562 cells

findings.claim: Bergman: intrinsic enhancer and promoter activities combine multiplicatively, R2 = 0.82 (so about 18% of variance is left for interactions or noise: my arithmetic 1-0.82)
findings.evidence_quote: intrinsic enhancer and promoter activities combine multiplicatively to determine RNA output ( R 2 =0.82)

findings.claim: Bergman: most enhancers keep the same relative effect across promoters; mean Spearman between promoters 0.81, between enhancers 0.72 (so rank order is largely preserved)
findings.evidence_quote: with an average Spearman correlation across all pairs of promoters = 0.81 ( Fig. 2a , c , Extended Data Fig. 2c ), and pairs of enhancers showed similar proportional activation of promoters

findings.claim: Bergman: a rank-order-changing minority exists: enhancer cluster E1 (n=126) activates promoter cluster P1 (n=192) 1.93-fold more than P2 (n=391); E2 (n=290) activates both about equally (1.05-fold)
findings.value: 1.93-fold, P=4.19e-08 (t-test) for E1; 1.05-fold, P=0.424 for E2
findings.evidence_quote: E1 enhancer sequences activated P1 promoters more strongly than P2 promoters (by 1.93-fold, P = 4.19e-08, t -test), whereas E2 enhancer sequences activated promoters in both clusters approximately equally

findings.claim: Bergman: housekeeping-type (P2) promoters carry built-in GABPA/YY1 motifs and respond less to enhancers; responsiveness to E1 enhancers falls with intrinsic promoter activity in a way that appeared to saturate
findings.evidence_quote: responsiveness to E1 enhancers was inversely correlated with intrinsic promoter activity, in a way that appeared to saturate

findings.claim: Bergman: luciferase validation (enhancer 1 kb upstream) gave a multiplicative model explaining 84% of variance
findings.evidence_quote: a multiplicative function of enhancer and promoter activities explained 84% of the total variance in the measurements

findings.claim: Bergman data accession: GEO GSE184426 (ExP STARR-seq, motif ExP, HS STARR-seq, PRO-seq); code zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.6514733
findings.evidence_quote: Raw and processed data for ExP STARR-seq, motif ExP STARR-seq, HS STARR-seq, and K562 PRO-seq can be found in NCBI GEO under accession number GSE184426

findings.claim: Martinez-Ara 2022: mESC, 3 loci (Nanog, Tfcp2l1, Klf2), 82-192 cCREs and 18-25 promoters per locus; 10,678 cCRE-P pairs (with orientation) in Upstream assay, 1,364 in Downstream assay (10 Klf2 promoters)
findings.evidence_quote: in the three Upstream assays combined we tested a total of 10,678 cCRE-P pairs, or 3,747 pairs if we do not take orientations into account.

findings.claim: Martinez-Ara: 139 of 233 cCREs (59.9% as stated; 139/233 = 59.7% by my arithmetic) with >5 tested pairs show promoter selectivity beyond noise (ANOVA, FDR 5%)
findings.evidence_quote: out of 233 cCREs with more than 5 tested cCRE-P combinations, a total of 139 (59.9%) showed significant unexplained variance at an estimated false discovery rate (FDR) cutoff of 5%

findings.claim: Martinez-Ara re-analysis of Bergman K562 data: 90.46% of cCREs show boost-index variance above noise at 0.1% FDR. Disagreement of emphasis: Bergman stresses broad compatibility and multiplicativity, Martinez-Ara stresses widespread selectivity in the same data
findings.evidence_quote: for the majority of cCREs (90.46% at 0.1% FDR cutoff) the variance of boost indices was significantly larger than could be explained by experimental noise

findings.claim: Martinez-Ara: boosting strongest at weak-basal promoters; high-activity promoters hard to boost: saturation, or less dependence on distal enhancers
findings.evidence_quote: Strong boosting occurred primarily at promoters with low basal activities, while highly active promoters were more difficult to boost

findings.claim: Martinez-Ara: housekeeping vs developmental split only rough in mESC: housekeeping promoters have similar cCRE preferences; non-housekeeping promoters diverse, as different from each other as from housekeeping
findings.evidence_quote: the cCRE specificities of the non-housekeeping promoters are much more diverse and generally as distinct from each other as from the housekeeping promoters

findings.claim: Martinez-Ara 2022 accession: GEO GSE186265; code github vansteensellab/EPCombinations, zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.6406791
findings.evidence_quote: Raw sequencing data and processed data are available at Gene expression Omnibus (GEO): GSE186265

findings.claim: Martinez-Ara 2024 (eLife): about 69,000 enhancer-enhancer-promoter combinations, 7 developmental promoters + 1 housekeeping promoter (Ap1m1) in mESC; enhancer pairs combine near-additively, promoters scale the sum non-linearly depending on promoter strength; housekeeping promoter has a different, smaller dynamic range
findings.evidence_quote: enhancer pairs generally combine near-additively. This behaviour was conserved across seven developmental promoters tested. Surprisingly, these promoters scale the enhancer signals in a non-linear manner that depends on promoter strength.

findings.claim: Martinez-Ara 2024: some saturation with the strongest enhancers; accession GEO GSE240586
findings.evidence_quote: although some saturation appears to occur with the strongest enhancers

findings.claim: Zabidi 2015: Drosophila S2 STARR-seq with two core promoters (housekeeping RpS12 vs developmental DSCP); 5,956 hk enhancers, 5,408 dev enhancers; genome-wide enhancer-activity profile PCC only 0.38
findings.evidence_quote: the genome-wide enhancer activity profiles differed (PCC 0.38), as did the individual enhancer strengths

findings.claim: Zabidi: of 11,364 enhancers, 8,144 (72%; my arithmetic 8144/11364 = 71.7%) activated one core promoter at least 2-fold more than the other: the strongest evidence for rank-order change in this literature
findings.evidence_quote: of the 11,364 enhancers, 8,144 (72%) activated one core promoter at least 2-fold more strongly than the other

findings.claim: Zabidi: luciferase validation: 21 of 24 hkCP-specific enhancers activated hkCP vs 1 from dCP; classes confirmed for five additional core promoters; DREF binds housekeeping enhancers, Trl/GAGA developmental ones
findings.evidence_quote: 21 out of 24 hkCP-specific enhancers activated luciferase expression (>1.5-fold and t -test P <0.05) from the hkCP versus 1 from the dCP

findings.claim: Zabidi accessions: GEO GSE40739 and GSE57876
findings.evidence_quote: deposited in the Gene Expression Omnibus database under the accession numbers GSE40739 and GSE57876

findings.claim: Haberle 2019: STAP-seq in Drosophila S2 screened 23 cofactors (COFs) against 72,000 candidate core promoters; COFs differ in which core-promoter types they activate (TATA, DPE, TCT groups; 5 CP clusters by k-means); 12,000 human CP candidates
findings.evidence_quote: screen 23 COFs for their ability to activate 72,000 candidate core promoters (CPs). We observe differential activation of CPs

findings.claim: Haberle: developmental and housekeeping enhancers preferentially activate Group 1/2 vs Group 3/4 core promoters, tying enhancer-CP specificity to cofactor-CP compatibility (no single fold number read from text)
findings.value: qualitative; Extended Data Fig 8c-f not readable here
findings.evidence_quote: developmental and housekeeping enhancers indeed preferentially activated Group 1 and 2 versus Group 3 and 4 CPs, respectively, when tested by STAP-seq

findings.claim: Haberle accessions: GEO GSE116197 (Drosophila), GSE126221 (human)
findings.evidence_quote: deposited in the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) under accession number GSE116197 ( D. melanogaster data) and GSE126221 (human data)

findings.claim: Arnold 2017 STAP-seq: with one strong enhancer, responsiveness of different genomic sequences as core promoters differs by several orders of magnitude (one enhancer, whole genome of candidate promoters)
findings.value: orders of magnitude (value not stated in abstract)
findings.evidence_quote: In the presence of a single strong enhancer, the enhancer responsiveness of different sequences differs by several orders of magnitude

findings.claim: Zuin 2022: enhancer effect is a nonlinear function of enhancer-promoter contact probability (hundreds of mESC lines, one fixed promoter)
findings.evidence_quote: the transcriptional effect of an enhancer depends on its contact probabilities with the promoter through a nonlinear relationship

findings.claim: EXTRA-seq (preprint 2024): TATA-box acts as a dynamic-range amplifier, modulating expression in function of enhancer strength (engineered enhancer-promoter combinations, genome-integrated)
findings.value: abstract only; no numbers or accession read
findings.evidence_quote: we reveal that the TATA-box acts as a dynamic range amplifier, modulating expression levels in function of enhancer strength.

findings.claim: Long-range MPRA (Cohen lab preprint 2025): over 300 K562 enhancers at distances to 100 kb with three promoters (HBE, HBG, GAPDH); long-range activity set mainly by enhancer strength, but also by promoter responsiveness
findings.evidence_quote: long-range enhancer-promoter interactions rely on not only enhancer properties but also promoter responsiveness

findings.claim: SPIE-seq / Regulation-by-Partition (2026 preprint): 724 clonal lines, 29,954 insertions, 18,440 enhancer-gene pairs; an enhancer allocates output among competing promoters; promoter skipping incompatible with independent promoters
findings.evidence_quote: Promoter skipping is common and increases as competitors accumulate - a pattern incompatible with promoters responding independently based solely on their intrinsic features.

key_claims.claim: In human K562 cells (1,000 x 1,000 design) most enhancers scale all promoters by similar fold-changes and a multiplicative model explains R2=0.82, so the rank order of enhancers is largely preserved across promoters.
key_claims.evidence_quote: intrinsic enhancer and promoter activities combine multiplicatively to determine RNA output ( R 2 =0.82)

key_claims.claim: The clearest rank-order change is between promoter classes: in Drosophila 72% of 11,364 enhancers prefer one of two core promoters by at least 2-fold (housekeeping vs developmental).
key_claims.evidence_quote: of the 11,364 enhancers, 8,144 (72%) activated one core promoter at least 2-fold more strongly than the other

key_claims.claim: Even in the multiplicative human data a structured minority deviates (E1/P1 1.93-fold), and the same K562 data show selectivity beyond noise by another group's test (90.46% of cCREs).
key_claims.evidence_quote: for the majority of cCREs (90.46% at 0.1% FDR cutoff) the variance of boost indices was significantly larger than could be explained by experimental noise

key_claims.claim: Promoter strength rescales enhancer input non-linearly (weak promoters boosted most; saturation at strong promoters and strongest enhancers), a mechanism that can reorder enhancers across promoters.
key_claims.evidence_quote: these promoters scale the enhancer signals in a non-linear manner that depends on promoter strength.

could_not_find: Per-pair rank-order statistics (for example Kendall tau of enhancers across each promoter pair) for any study except Bergman's mean Spearman; this needs re-analysis of the GEO tables (GSE184426, GSE186265, GSE240586), which I did not download.
Full text of the EXTRA-seq and long-range MPRA preprints (bioRxiv returned HTTP 429); only abstracts read, so no numbers or accessions for them.
A fold-number for Haberle 2019 enhancer-versus-core-promoter group preference: it is in Extended Data Fig 8c-f, which I could not read as values.
Zabidi 2015 values for the five additional core promoters beyond the statement that the two classes were confirmed.

No 2023-2026 crossed enhancer x promoter MPRA beyond Martinez-Ara 2024 and the 2025-2026 preprints; search was Europe PMC title and abstract queries only (OpenAlex not used), so coverage may be incomplete.
Bergman's Extended Data figures were not read, so the saturation curve has no numbers.

The Nature Reviews MCB 2024 review (10.1038/s41580-024-00710-6) and the Nature 2025 lentiMPRA paper (10.1038/s41586-024-08430-9) were seen but not used: the first not read, the second not a crossed design.
